name: stand_up_pinch_flip_vertical
code:
def primitive(obj, target, p):
    # Lying object: pinch one end from above, lift and rotate hand to flip vertical
    cx, cy = obj['center']
    yaw = obj['axis_yaw']
    major = obj['extent_major']
    minor = obj['extent_minor']
    height = obj['height']
    
    # Choose which end to grasp (parameter selects end)
    end_offset = p['end_choice'] * major / 2.0
    grasp_x = cx + end_offset * cos(yaw)
    grasp_y = cy + end_offset * sin(yaw)
    
    # Orient hand so fingers pinch across the minor axis
    # Hand x-axis along long axis, fingers open/close perpendicular to it
    grip_yaw = yaw
    
    open_gripper()
    
    # Approach from above
    approach_z = height + p['approach_height']
    move(grasp_x, grasp_y, approach_z, yaw=grip_yaw, speed=0.2)
    
    # Lower to grasp height (slightly above table to grip the cylinder)
    grasp_z = height * p['grasp_height_ratio']
    move(grasp_x, grasp_y, grasp_z, yaw=grip_yaw, speed=0.1)
    
    # Close to pinch the end
    close_gripper(force=p['grip_force'])
    wait(0.3)
    
    if not holding():
        return False
    
    # Lift up while keeping horizontal
    lift_z = p['lift_height']
    move(grasp_x, grasp_y, lift_z, yaw=grip_yaw, pitch=0.0, speed=0.08)
    wait(0.2)
    
    # Now rotate the hand to flip object vertical
    # Pitch rotates about the line between fingertips
    # Positive pitch swings the object up along the hand's x direction
    flip_pitch = p['flip_angle']
    move(grasp_x, grasp_y, lift_z, yaw=grip_yaw, pitch=flip_pitch, speed=0.06)
    wait(0.3)
    
    # Move to where the object's base should touch down
    # After flipping, the object extends down from the gripper
    # Estimate how far below the TCP the bottom will be
    set_down_z = p['set_down_height']
    move(grasp_x, grasp_y, set_down_z, yaw=grip_yaw, pitch=flip_pitch, speed=0.05)
    wait(0.2)
    
    # Release
    open_gripper()
    wait(0.2)
    retreat(dz=0.1)
    
    return True
description: Pinch one end of the lying object from above, lift it, then rotate the hand 90 degrees using pitch to flip the object vertical, and lower it to stand on its end.
check: object is upright (height increased significantly, width decreased)

approach_height.meaning: height above object to approach from (m)

grasp_height_ratio.meaning: fraction of object height to grasp at

lift_height.meaning: how high to lift before flipping (m)

flip_angle.meaning: pitch angle to flip object vertical (radians, ~90 deg)

set_down_height.meaning: TCP height when setting object down (m)

lineage.description: stand an object that lies on its side (fallen over) back up on one of its ends, where it lies; its long axis must end vertical
